title: Christian magi on the Blessings
summary: How the Messianic Voices see inquisitor powers.

claims.text: Christian magi of the Messianic Voices tend to see inquisitors who use showy Endowments as hedge wizards working theurgy through faith, or even as fellow magi.
Their attitude ranges from pride in a shared cause to rivalry or mild scorn for overzealous younger siblings.
The Voices’ angelic magic outstrips all but the greatest Endowments, and some see both as gifts along one continuum of God-given talent.

title: Curses seen as signs of grace

claims.text: Many inquisitors do not see their Curses as curses at all: stigmata mark the sufferer as Christ-like, and speaking in tongues proves the Holy Spirit within.
The Church holds the stigmata to be extraordinarily holy, and the Red Order bears most of the Stigmata Curses, some with gratitude.
Developing a new Endowment usually takes a retreat of a week to a month, set by player and Storyteller according to its power.
On retreat an inquisitor may bank more than the usual one Conviction point a day, up to the highest Superior Virtue plus its controlling Virtue, still rolling for prayer as normal.
Rushing advancement through Conviction alone draws Curses; a single Curse is easily forgiven, several mark a rash inquisitor.
The inquisitor usually feels dread at once after the prideful act, and the Curse takes hold within about a day.

title: Pulling the Serpent’s Fangs
summary: An Advocate-level Legacy of House Murnau.

claims.text: The Faith version costs a Conviction point and a Manipulation + Faith roll at difficulty 6, striking every supernatural foe in sight mute for three turns per success and breaking spoken effects such as Dominate or incantations.
The Wisdom version, Charisma + Wisdom at difficulty 6, forces a creature of darkness to spend a Willpower point per success each time it tries to act against the inquisitor for the scene.
The Zeal version puts a target’s reasoning side to sleep: vampires and werewolves frenzy, magi fall asleep and fae react unpredictably.

title: Psalms of the Sisters
summary: Two Psalms of the Sisters of St. John.

claims.text: One facet lets a Sister in skin contact with a restrained creature sing its thoughts aloud, for two Conviction and Perception + Wisdom at difficulty 6, or 8 if the creature knows no human language.
The Zeal facet, called Dies Irae, costs two Conviction and Charisma + Zeal at difficulty 7, bringing down divine fire, wind and lightning on every place in earshot that shelters Lucifer’s minions.
With two or more successes the cleansed place becomes Holy Ground with an Ambient Faith equal to the successes for a week, but the Sister takes a level of unsoakable bashing damage per success.

title: A rite to hide the faithful
summary: A Holy Art ritual that masks an inquisitor from supernatural senses.

claims.text: Over an hour of silent prayer the inquisitor is anointed with oils; each success on the roll at difficulty 7 adds one to the difficulty of supernatural attempts to see the inquisitor as more than an ordinary person.
Under it, powers such as Soul Sight show no special aura and even strong emotions are muted.
It lasts one hour per success plus one more per Conviction spent; some in the Church think a rite that hides the presence of God is somewhat sinful.

title: Tears of the Weeping Heart of Abel
summary: A level three Holy Art ritual that strengthens holy water.

claims.text: Agents of the shadow Inquisition in the Church hierarchy make sure some blessed water passes through their hands to receive this extra rite.

Starting with conventionally blessed water, on Holy Ground if performed alone, the inquisitor makes a thirty-minute Intelligence + Theology roll at difficulty 6, then spends one Conviction per vial and prays for thirty more minutes.
The result is a weapon against Satan’s minions that anyone can wield.
